Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit evals & open-model parity next steps

Hi Evan / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the immediate next steps for the model-fit evaluation we discussed. TL;DR: we recommended running two open-model candidates (OpenLM-3-small, OpenLM-3-medium quantized) against your proprietary baseline for the set of customer-facing summary tasks you demoed.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Primary goal: match or beat current proprietary baseline on extractive accuracy and concise summarization while keeping token cost under $0.002/token equivalent.
- Target evals: canonical prompts for account summaries, refund triage, and 2-step escalation triage.
- Acceptance thresholds (initial suggestion):
  - Summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.78 relative to baseline
  - Extractive precision >= 0.82
  - Latency P95 <= 450ms for 512-token windows (on dedicated capacity)
- Quality regression concerns: you're right to flag hallucination on rare entities — we'll include focused prompt sets and stress tests for entity recall.

Attachments & links:
- Attached: prompt_set_v1.json (canonical prompts + edge-case prompts), parity_benchmarks_20270712.xlsx (sample evaluation matrix), eval_run_20270712.log (example run).
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdSharedDriveLink (detailed eval plan & scripts).

Immediate next steps (ownership & timing):
1) PayGrid to drop a 1-week sample of anonymized transcripts for the eval (Evan) — target: by end of week (7/16).
2) Redwood to run the initial parity sweep on OpenLM-3-small/medium (Marissa) — results within 3 business days of dataset receipt.
3) If parity is close but below thresholds, follow-up with quantization/temperature + prompt-tuning suggestions (Aditya + Marissa).

Can you confirm the data delivery timeline? Also flag any constraints for running on dedicated capacity (e.g., IP allowlist or contract access).

Thanks — look forward to the dataset.

—
Lauren Bishop

Evan / team —

Following up on Lauren's plan with a bit more of the technical approach and acceptance criteria so everyone is aligned before the dataset lands. Quick bullets:

- Models to run (initial): OpenLM-3-small (fp16), OpenLM-3-medium (int8 quant), Proprietary-baseline (PayGrid-provided eval).
- Evaluation metrics: ROUGE-L, BLEU (for structured response tasks), entity F1 for named entities, and a hallucination score (precision of asserted facts). We'll produce a per-task scoring sheet in the shared drive.
- Parity thresholds (recommended, can be tuned):
  * Summarization ROUGE-L: >= 0.78 relative to baseline
  * Entity F1 (critical customer fields): >= 0.80 absolute
  * Hallucination precision: >= 0.90
  * Cost: <= 65% of baseline token-cost (measured on Redwood Dedicated price points)
- Stress tests: out-of-vocabulary company names, multi-turn context collapse (long 10+ turns), truncated context windows.

If initial runs fall within +/-3% on primary metrics but exceed cost, our suggested next steps are: prompt engineering + light distillation (Aditya), quantization tuning (we have recipes for int8->int4 flows), and a follow-up targeted eval with adversarial prompts.

I'll prepare a results template so you can see per-example diffs and flagged hallucinations. Expect the first report within 72 hours of receiving the dataset.

One ask on governance: please include who at PayGrid can approve retention for the dataset in case we need to keep logs for debugging (we keep everything encrypted and access-controlled).

Thanks — looking forward to the data.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
